Team — below are three concrete drafting options and short, realistic examples to send to Acme. I attached a compiled doc with the redlines (draft_clauses_redwood_v1.docx) and highlighted the positions we feel comfortable taking.

Summary guidance (short):
- Keep consequential exclusions broad (lost profits, business interruption, loss of goodwill, reputational harm).
- Preserve a carve-out for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct and (ii) breach of confidentiality or IP infringement.
- For data loss, split recovery: direct remediation costs (data restoration, forensics, reasonable engineering time, express customer notification costs) are permitted as "direct" damages up to a correlated cap; consequential damages tied to lost business/reputation remain excluded.

Option A — Seller-favorable (recommended when we need firm cap discipline)
1) LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM (A) WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS FOR THIRD-PARTY IP INFRINGEMENT, AND (C) BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE AMOUNTS PAID BY CUSTOMER TO SELLER IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY OR (II) TWO MILLION DOLLARS (USD 2,000,000). CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, AND EXEMPLARY DAMAGES (INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, LOST PROFITS OR LOSS OF GOODWILL) ARE DISCLAIMED AND EXCLUDED.

Option B — Balanced (middle ground)
1) LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM (A) WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS FOR THIRD-PARTY IP INFRINGEMENT, AND (C) BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE AMOUNTS PAID BY CUSTOMER TO SELLER IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY OR (II) FIVE MILLION DOLLARS (USD 5,000,000). CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, AND EXEMPLARY DAMAGES (INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, LOST PROFITS OR LOSS OF GOODWILL) ARE DISCLAIMED AND EXCLUDED. NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, REASONABLE DIRECT COSTS INCURRED TO RESTORE OR RECOVER CUSTOMER DATA OR TO PERFORM FORENSIC INVESTIGATION SHALL BE RECOVERABLE BUT SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE LIMIT SET FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ABOVE.

Option C — Customer-favorable (what Acme is effectively requesting)
1) LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM (A) WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS FOR THIRD-PARTY IP INFRINGEMENT, AND (C) BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED TEN MILLION DOLLARS (USD 10,000,000) OR THE AMOUNTS PAID BY CUSTOMER TO SELLER IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY, WHICHEVER IS GREATER. CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, AND EXEMPLARY DAMAGES (INCLUDING LOST PROFITS OR LOSS OF GOODWILL) ARE DISCLAIMED AND EXCLUDED. DATA RESTORATION, FORENSICS, AND REASONABLE THIRD-PARTY REMEDIATION COSTS SHALL BE TREATED AS DIRECT DAMAGES AND ARE RECOVERABLE.

Examples to illustrate direct vs indirect (short):
- Lost profits from a delayed product launch: indirect/consequential — excluded.
- Loss of customer goodwill after press coverage of an outage: consequential — excluded.
- Corruption of production dataset requiring restoration from backups and forensics costs: treated as direct (limited to actual restoration and third-party forensic fees), recoverable up to direct-damage cap.
- Billing errors that directly overcharge customer and require immediate refund: direct, recoverable.

Practical negotiation notes:
- If Acme insists on higher cap, push for time-limited escalation (e.g., customer can opt into an enhanced cap for the first 12 months post-signing with a one-time fee or higher order form commitment).
- Avoid a blanket carve-out for "data loss" that includes reputational or downstream business interruption losses.

Ask: approve Option B as a starting point with a fallback to Option A if Acme refuses. If Sales prefers to give ground on cap, consider the enhanced-cap-for-fee approach (Karthik, can you model a one-time surcharge that yields $2.5M incremental expected liability buffer?).

Attachments: draft_clauses_redwood_v1.docx (with tracked redline and inline commentary).

Vivek / team — thanks for the clear options and the worked examples. Acme prefers Option B but would like explicit language that data restoration costs are recoverable even if the root cause is a non-willful bug (so long as the bug is caused by Redwood's product or change). We can accept the cap at $5M if we get the broader data remediation carve-out.
